title: Turning Veo clips into turn-based battle animations for my solo Godot RPG (what worked, what broke)
author: Careless_Road8873
selftext:
I'm making SOFT (Survival Of the Fittest: Thrones), a free medieval sandbox RPG in Godot 4: you start as a nobody with a club and a few coins, build a band, take jobs, and maybe end up holding a realm. It's a one-person project, and I lean on AI for both code and art, so I wanted to share how the battle animations work, because that part took the most trial and error.

The art pipeline: I paint the fighters as stills, then animate a swing, a block, a dodge, a fall with Veo, using the still as the start frame. A script cuts the video into frames, keys out the background, matches brightness to the first frame so the clip doesn't flash against the standing sprite, and packs it into an atlas with a small meta file (anchor point, duration, the frame where the hit lands). In battle the clip plays over the unit and the still fades back in when it ends.

The hard part was weapons. A clip is generated with one sword, but in the game a fighter might carry an axe, a mace or a dagger. So the script tracks the blade through the clip (hilt and tip in every frame) and the game draws the fighter's actual weapon along that line. Tracking worked well on cloth and leather. On mail and plate it failed: shiny armour looks like a blade to the tracker, so for those I'm placing the sword by hand frame by frame. If anyone has a better trick for that, I'd love to hear it.

Another lesson: the web build. All those painted frames pushed one pack past itch.io's 200 MB file limit. I split the art into three packs that download after the game starts, so the first load is under 90 MB and the animations arrive while you're on the map.

For code, most of it is written with Claude, while I design, test and review. What made that work for me: every finding gets checked against the code before anything changes, and every change gets tests and a screenshot or short video before it goes into the build.

Happy to answer questions about any part of the pipeline. The game is free to play in the browser: https://gadavra.itch.io/soft
